g.text: OpenAlex / Crossref RAG + Study Design Badges
Walker, Mander, Archer • 2017 • Nature Rev Neuro
Sleep loss impairs prefrontal cortical control
Baseline stress and HPA hyperarousal precede
GWAS loci for habitual sleep duration
🛡️ Collider Guard Active: Conditioning on 'Campus Clinic Visit' is blocked to prevent Berkson's bias.
📓 Living Research Notebook & Protocol Synthesis (Split View)
To estimate the total effect of Chronic Sleep Deprivation (X) on Cognitive Performance (Y),
we adjust for baseline HPA-axis stress (Kalmbach et al., 2018) and night shift schedules.
We explicitly avoid conditioning on Prefrontal Executive Fatigue (Walker et al., 2017) as it
mediates the primary pathway X → M → Y (preventing overadjustment bias).
Export ready: DAGitty syntax • R (ggdag) • Python (DoWhy) • LaTeX (TikZ)
Modes: Socratic • Devil's Advocate • Lit Scout
Habitual evening caffeine (t₀) confounds sleep onset,
whereas reactive daytime caffeine (t₂) is a mediator.
Should we control for students visiting the campus
health clinic in our regression model?
Hold on! In your DAG, both Sleep Loss (X) and
Exam Distress (Y) point into Clinic Visit:
Sleep Loss → Clinic Visit ← Exam Score
That makes Clinic Visit a Collider. Conditioning
on it opens a spurious biasing path (Berkson's bias)!
💬 How do we test if baseline anxiety (t₀) confounds X and Y?
💬 Find cohort studies testing shift work → sleep loss
